name: STM32 Blue Pill
summary: The ubiquitous unbranded STM32F103C8 board: a 72 MHz Cortex-M3 for a couple of dollars, with well-known quirks.

chip.value: STMicroelectronics STM32F103C8 (often a clone or relabelled part)

usb.value: Micro-USB to the chip’s USB device peripheral

docs.label: STM32F103C8 product page and datasheet, STMicroelectronics

gotchas.title: Wrong USB pull-up resistor
gotchas.text: Many boards fit a 10 kΩ pull-up on USB D+ instead of 1.5 kΩ, which makes USB unreliable on some hosts.

gotchas.title: Counterfeit chips
gotchas.text: Cheap boards often carry clone chips (CKS32, CS32 and others) that differ in subtle ways and may fail ST's programming tools.

gotchas.title: No USB bootloader out of the box
gotchas.text: The STM32F103 has no USB DFU in ROM; first programming needs a serial adapter or an ST-LINK.

editorial.history: Sold by many Chinese vendors from about 2015, the Blue Pill made 32-bit Arm affordable for hobbyists, helped by the community STM32duino core.
editorial.today: Still cheap, but the WeAct Black Pill (STM32F411) and RP2040 boards avoid most of its quirks for similar money.
